extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners subject to USPTO enrollment and discipline; OED staff; disciplinary agencies
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline based on a state bar suspension, describing service, opportunity to respond, findings, publication, and duties during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner that is identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State (here, suspension for six (6) months by the Supreme Court of the State of Nevada).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order sought imposition of 'reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the November 17, 2022 Order of the Supreme Court of the State of Nevada.' The Final Order determined that identical suspension from practice of trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO for six (6) months is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose and 40-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the State order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent of the 40-day deadline to oppose based on reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Respondent's failure to file a response was deemed to create 'no genuine issue of material fact' under § 11.24(d) and supported imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references these permitted grounds as the exclusive bases for opposition but does not list them verbatim; because Respondent did not respond, none were asserted and the Office found no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail to the Respondent; if delivery cannot be made, the Notice and Order is published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here the Notice and Order (sent certified mail, receipt no. 70220410000250016985) was not deliverable and therefore was published in the Official Gazette on November 21, 2023 and November 28, 2023. The Final Order must also be electronically published at OED's FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification of public discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication in the Official Gazette, posting in the FOIA/OED reading room, and notice to relevant disciplinary agencies and courts as required by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of a suspended practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order instructs Respondent to follow the post-discipline obligations set out in § 11.58 (the Order does not reproduce those duties but requires compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these provisions as the legal basis authorizing the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish disciplinary decisions for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law professional-conduct violations as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nevada suspension was predicated upon violations of the Nevada Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.1 (competence), 1.2 (scope of representation and allocation of authority between client and lawyer), 1.3 (diligence), 1.4 (communication), 1.5 (fees), 1.15 (safekeeping property), 1.16 (declining or terminating representation), 3.2 (expediting litigation), and 8.1 (bar admission and disciplinary matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains these violations arose from failing to perform work for two clients (including failing to appear at a court hearing and file documents), failing to keep clients apprised or respond to communications, and failing to respond to State Bar inquiries. Such state-law findings formed the factual basis for reciprocal suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prohibited practice during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes Respondent 'is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters' (i.e., the suspension specifically covers trademark and non-patent practice; patent-practice authorization status is separately noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to electronically publish the Final Order at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ and references the FOIA reading room location for public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed to the Respondent (certified mail, return receipt requested) and a certificate of service included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a Certificate of Service showing mailing to the Respondent at the address listed by the American Bar Association, with date and USPTO mailing address provided.
